title: AIADMK Fractures Live on Assembly Floor
excerpt: Two rival factions submit competing letters to Tamil Nadu's Pro-tem Speaker, each naming a different legislature party leader.
body:
Tamil Nadu's 55-year-old opposition party AIADMK fractured publicly on May 11, 2026 — the very first day of the 17th Legislative Assembly — as two hostile factions arrived in separate groups, submitted rival letters, and named different men as their legislature party leader.

**What happened on the assembly floor:**
While 17 MLAs submitted a letter on the morning of May 11 seeking the appointment of Edappadi K. Palaniswami as AIADMK Legislature Party Leader, another faction led by C.V. Shanmugam submitted a separate letter in the evening demanding that S.P. Velumani be recognised as Leader of the Legislature Party. The internal conflict became visible on the very first day of the Assembly as AIADMK legislators reportedly arrived in separate groups for the oath-taking ceremony.

**How the crisis reached this point:**
Even during a meeting of party MLAs held on May 9 at Palaniswami's residence on Greenways Road in Chennai, no final decision was reached, and sources claim Palaniswami eventually told the Shanmugam faction to 'do as you wish.' Tensions escalated further during another round of talks on the night of May 10, which reportedly ended on a bitter note. The AIADMK, which led the NDA alliance, finished third behind TVK and DMK in the Tamil Nadu Assembly polls, having contested 169 constituencies but winning only 47 seats as the debutant TVK clinched power.

**The anti-defection arithmetic:**
The ongoing crisis has brought India's anti-defection law into focus: at least two-thirds of the legislature party must support a split for MLAs to avoid disqualification. In the AIADMK's case, the rebel faction would require support from at least 32 of the party's 47 MLAs — and reports suggest the dissident camp currently has the backing of around 30, leaving them just two members short.

**What to watch next:**
The conduct of Shanmugam and other AIADMK MLAs points to an impending split, and one of the factions is expected to openly support the TVK government when the vote of confidence is taken in the House on May 13.
